item.title: TCB At The EOC
item.description: An elderly woman reported that her neighbor's contractor was shoveling snow onto her yard. A woman said her car wasn't able to get out of Warren Street. Someone said that his neighbor's car was blocking the road on Fairfield Street. All those calls and more were answered Monday at the city's Emergency Operations Center (EOC). The post TCB At The EOC appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: The Day After The Blizzard: A “Wet & Heavy” 20 Inches; 242 Cars Towed So Far
item.description: Up to 20 inches of "really wet and heavy" snow fell on New Haven between Sunday and Monday -- leading to three ambulances and several plows getting stuck, and 242 vehicles being towed for violating the city's parking ban. The post The Day After The Blizzard: A “Wet & Heavy” 20 Inches; 242 Cars Towed So Far appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: Another Snow Day Spells Longer School Year
item.description: New Haven's public school district can't say for sure when the current school year will end -- now that a blizzard has canceled classes for two days in a row, requiring the city to make up those days in June. The post Another Snow Day Spells Longer School Year appeared first on New Haven Independent.

item.title: Fire Breaks Out At 5-Story Building
item.description: Firefighters rescued 11 people -- including three who were hanging out of upper-floor windows -- after responding to a three-alarm blaze at a five-story apartment building near the corner of Chapel Street and Winthrop Avenue midday Tuesday. The post Fire Breaks Out At 5-Story Building appeared first on New Haven Independent.
